stories.name: Sample: a student
stories.headline: Chose computer science after the quiz put Investigative first
stories.story: I had picked my subjects for the wrong reason — everyone in my class was applying for the same thing. The quiz put Investigative and Realistic at the top and I recognised myself in it immediately: I liked taking things apart more than presenting about them. The flight plan told me to learn one language properly before touching frameworks, which I ignored for two months and then came back to. It was right.

stories.name: Sample: a graduate
stories.headline: Two matches were within three points, and that was the useful part
stories.story: The result would not pick between design and front-end development, and instead of hiding that it told me the real difference was how much open-ended creative work I wanted in a day. That was a question I could actually answer. I shadowed a designer for a week and knew within two days.

stories.name: Sample: a professional
stories.headline: Changed direction at thirty-one without starting over
stories.story: I assumed a change meant throwing away eight years in operations. The match came back Data Analyst and the reasoning pointed at the part of my job I already liked — finding out why the numbers disagreed. Most of what the roadmap asked for was evenings, not a degree.
